newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices fall but turnover rises.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices fall but turnover rises.

text.p: Cements, mills and real estate shares stole the action in higher turnover in the Cairo stock market on Wednesday, but most prices closed lower.
Out of the 88 shares traded, 43 ended down, 25 rose and 20 were unchanged in 74.8 million pounds ($22 million) turnover, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.
The all-share index fell 5.56 points to 374.4.
"Volumes were good today but a lot of prices did go down," said broker Dalia Sultan of EFG-Hermes. "They probably went down due to the holidays in the past weeks."
The bourse will be closed on Thursday for the first day of the Islamic calendar new year.

Suez Cement shares fell, as did most of the other cements, but it was in the limelight as the day's top performer in terms of turnover with 5.6 million pounds changing hands. It closed down 0.77 at 67 pounds.
The second highest turnover resided in Upper Egypt Flour Mills trade of 5.4 million pounds. It rose 1.5 to 86.
That turnover was twice as high as Tuesday's trade.
The real estate sector weighed in with Heliopolis Housing and Development turnover of 4.7 million pounds. Its share price fell 3.99 to close at 408.01 pounds.
Then Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN notched up 4.2 million pounds turnover, and closed down 1.11 at 140.
"PACHIN is sustaining at high volumes. It's a good company," said Sultan.

Commercial International Bank (CIB), which led trade on Tuesday, was among at least four mixed stocks which exceeded 3 million pounds trade. CIB shares closed down again on Wednesday, slipping 2.89 to 77.11 pounds at the closing.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 544.78 points from 554.38 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 268.25 from 271.82.
